targetAudience.primary: Open-source maintainers building reusable agent, LLM and HTTP client runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands shallow copying, request configuration and reusable live clients.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Deep copying configuration crashes on live resources, while sharing all mutable options leaks per-call mutation into later invocations.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK change introduces mutation-specific HTTP option copying and narrow live-session restart copying.

externalHook.description: Isolation should follow the fields that are actually mutated, not recursively clone every live object reachable from configuration.

coreProposition: Reusable runtimes should snapshot request-mutable option containers per invocation while intentionally preserving live clients by reference; this copy-on-mutation boundary avoids demonstrated aliasing and cloning failures without pretending to provide deep isolation.

originalValue.description: Turns copying from a generic object operation into an explicit ownership contract for each configuration field.

readerTakeaway: Classify fields as invocation-mutable, immutable or shared live resources; copy only the first class before mutation and test both identity preservation and leak prevention.

supported: Headers, extra body, client args and async client args receive new dictionary containers.
Retry options receive a separate model copy.
Caller-supplied live HTTP clients remain shared by identity while demonstrated container mutation is isolated.
uncertain: How future mutable fields are enrolled in the helper
Which nested values require stronger ownership rules

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article establishes a general mutable-state ownership pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The helper implementation and identity/mutation regressions support a practical, bounded copy-on-mutation pattern.
